raw_response:
I'm a 60-year-old man, been farming these same two mu in Quzhou for forty years. Middle school education — back then that was enough to read the county bulletins and talk to the extension fellow when he comes around, but most of what I know comes from doing it myself year after year. My wife and I are the main hands now. Our son works in Shijiazhuang and sends a bit home, but I don't like touching that money for the fields. This farm has to pay for itself.

Two mu isn't much, but it's what we have. Every jin of seed and every bag of fertilizer has to be counted. I've got maybe eight hundred yuan in cash I can put into inputs for the whole year, and I need to keep some aside for my wife's medicine and for the pump repairs if the well breaks again. So I can't afford to be generous, but I also know that skimping too much is false economy. Three years ago I tried saving fifty yuan on fertilizer and the wheat turned yellow at jointing — lost almost a third of the yield. Never again.

**Winter wheat** — I plant the whole two mu. The extension pamphlet says 15 kg of nitrogen per mu, but I've found my soil needs a bit more than that to get the color right. I'll put down about 40 kg per mu of compound fertilizer — the 19-22-7 type from the co-op, costs about 130 yuan for a 50 kg bag. For two mu I'll need one and a half bags for the base. Then at jointing, if the wheat looks pale, I'll topdress with urea — about 15 kg per mu. That's another half bag. The seed I'll use is the improved variety I've been buying from the county store, not the fancy hybrids — 30 jin per mu, costs me about 20 yuan per mu since I save some from last year and just top up. I irrigate three times: once before winter to help the roots, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. The pump electricity is metered now and it's not cheap, but without it you're gambling on the rain, and I don't gamble with wheat — that's our staple money. One spraying of herbicide after planting, about 15 yuan per mu. I do the rotary till myself with the small tiller I bought fifteen years ago. Harvest is usually first week of June, and I expect about 400 kg per mu if the spring doesn't dry out.

**Summer maize** — the window between wheat harvest and maize planting is brutal. Sometimes only three or four days if the weather turns wet. I'll plant immediately after the wheat comes off, around June 10th. No time for fancy tillage — one quick pass with the rotary tiller, or no-till if the stubble isn't too thick. Maize has to be hybrid seed, you can't save it, so I buy from the seed dealer — about one package per mu, 50 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, everything goes down at planting. I'll put 50 kg per mu of compound fertilizer in the row — the 27-6-7 type, one bag does both mu. No time for split application, the season's too short. I irrigate twice if it's dry, but usually the summer rains help. I spray herbicide once and insecticide once — the corn borer was bad two years ago and I lost ears, so I don't skip that anymore. Harvest end of September, and I figure 450 kg per mu is reasonable.

Labor is all family. My wife and I can handle two mu. Hiring workers is 150 yuan a day now, and on this small plot there's no margin for that. The tradeoff is we work longer hours, but we keep the money in our pocket.
